AFDOHX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Nashville TN
600 AM CDT Thu Aug 27 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES...
Updated at 557 AM CDT Thu Aug 27 2026

- Areas of patchy dense fog through 9 am this morning, especially
  over southern Middle TN.

- Low to medium thunderstorm chances Thursday afternoon. Severe
  weather is not expected.

- Seasonable temperatures will warm into the mid and upper-90s
  next week with mostly dry conditions.

&&

.SHORT TERM...
(Tonight through Friday Night)
Issued at 1038 PM CDT Wed Aug 26 2026

A short wave trough is exiting to our southeast and we will see
short wave ridging build in overnight. This will bring a concern 
for fog, some of the fog could be dense with the highest chances
in southern and western areas. A Dense Fog Advisory may be needed
depending on how widespread the fog development is. 

A short wave trough exiting the Great Lakes will push a boundary 
south. This will push into the area overnight and will bring some 
cloud cover and a low shower chance before daybreak to the 
northwest part of the area. The boundary will slowly work east 
through the region as the day goes on. CAPE will increase to above
1000 j/kg by the afternoon with around 20 knots of bulk shear. 
The boundary will be enough forcing to kick off some scattered 
showers and thunderstorms with the highest chances east of I-65. 
Lapse rates will be poor and forcing with the boundary will only 
be marginal, this will keep the severe threat very low. Highs will
make it into the upper 80s to lower 90s. 

Showers and thunderstorms will diminish quickly after sunset and 
dry weather settles in Thursday night. Patchy fog will be a
concern once again with the highest chances for for fog over the
Plateau. Troughing will push to our east on Friday as the Four
Corners ridge amplifies. This will bring quiet and dry weather 
with highs in the mid 80s to lower 90s. 

&&

.LONG TERM...
(Saturday through next Thursday)
Issued at 1038 PM CDT Wed Aug 26 2026

The strong ridge to our west will slowly build east as we head
into the weekend. This will keep conditions dry with warming
temperatures. Highs will push into the low to mid 90s by Sunday.
By early next week the upper level ridge will be over us keeping
the warming trend going. We will see widespread highs in the low
to mid 90s with some upper 90s possible. The ridge will linger 
over the areas for much of the week keeping conditions hot. Rain 
chances will be very low throughout the week. 

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAFS)
Issued at 557 AM CDT Thu Aug 27 2026

Mixed bag of clouds and fog have led to IFR to MVFR cats this
morning. All should improve by 14Z as heating allows for clearing
back to VFR. Have added a few hours of PROB30 for BNA/MQY as
latest CAMs suggest late afternoon development along weak passing
frontal boundary. Winds will be very light and shift to the north
behind this boundary passage today.

&&

.PRELIMINARY POINT TEMPS/POPS...
Nashville      92  67  90  64 /  30  10   0   0 
Clarksville    90  64  88  62 /  10   0   0   0 
Crossville     86  63  84  60 /  40  20  10   0 
Columbia       93  67  91  64 /  30   0   0   0 
Cookeville     87  65  86  63 /  40  20   0   0 
Jamestown      86  65  84  62 /  40  20  10   0 
Lawrenceburg   90  66  89  63 /  30  10   0   0 
Murfreesboro   93  67  91  64 /  30  10   0   0 
Waverly        91  66  89  63 /  20   0   0   0 

&&

.OHX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...

Dense Fog Advisory until 9 AM CDT this morning for TNZ056>065-
075-077>080-093>095.

&&

$$

SHORT TERM...Mueller
LONG TERM....Mueller
AVIATION.....Unger
